statement: The valuation state tracks, per instrument, the last finite close observed at a run pulse (an open-session close inside the run window); a missing or non-finite close is no observation.
applies_to_paths: run; resume; sweep; walk_forward; promote; reconstruct; readers
notes: Bars that fall on no pulse are dropped before this state sees them (backtest-runner.R:1004-1023); that alignment belongs to subsystem 4.

statement: Mark age is the number of run pulses since the last observed close, so a held mark ages on the declared venue-open-session clock through halts and known inactivity.
applies_to_paths: run; resume; sweep; walk_forward; promote; readers
notes: Probe: FFF halted s14-s15 shows ages 1 and 2, then 0 at s16.

statement: A mark is permissible when its age is at most max_sessions; max_sessions = 0 admits only a current-session close.
applies_to_paths: run; resume; sweep; walk_forward; promote; readers

statement: Every axis ID gets one mark_source per pulse from the closed set current_close, stale_close, expired_close, missing and frozen_close.
notes: expired_close is a reference older than the horizon on an unheld or unfrozen ID; missing means no observation in the run window.

statement: Mark lookback is bounded by the run window: no close before the run's first pulse is visible, so an opening or carried holding whose instrument has no bar on the first pulse has no mark and stops the run at that pulse with valuation_horizon_exhausted, even when a recent pre-window close exists.
contract_heading: Result Contract (reconstruction: last observed close in the run window)
oddity: Opening FFF (last bar s13 close 20) dated s14 or s15 under stale(5) stops at its first pulse with mark_source missing; dated s13 it runs DONE.
notes: Walk-forward carry_test_state openings take this path (inferred, not probed). Sweep bars are fetched from range$warmup_start, equal to the scoring start since Cut 9.

statement: Availability-aware equity values every held position at its valuation mark (current, stale or frozen close) at each pulse; dense runs value at the raw pulse close.

Within one availability pulse the order is: post due corporate-action cash, resolve the decision view and marks, post due scheduled dispositions, resolve lifetime terminals, stop or freeze on exhausted marks, write the equity row, then build the strategy context.
notes: Cash posting sees raw closes (fold-engine.R:520) for affected_marked_exposure, not valuation marks.

statement: A held ID with no mark at all, or with an aged mark under exhausted = 'refuse', stops the run with valuation_horizon_exhausted before that pulse's equity row, so the last fully valued pulse is the previous one.
notes: Probe: stale(0) refuse, FFF missing s14: INCOMPLETE, last valued s13.

statement: Under exhausted = 'freeze' a held ID whose last close is older than max_sessions keeps that close as a frozen mark, is target-restricted with reason valuation_frozen appended, and returns to current_close on its next observed close.
applies_to_paths: run; resume; sweep; walk_forward; promote; readers
notes: Probe: freeze at s14-s15 with trading_halted|valuation_frozen, exit at s16 at 14.

statement: Freeze entry and exit are diagnostics only (valuation_frozen, valuation_freeze_exited); the frozen set for a resumed run is rebuilt at the last committed pulse from ledger holdings, sealed facts and bars, never stored.
A held ID covered by an effective and knowable known_inactive lifetime row is disposed or stopped by the terminal path before the freeze check, so it never freezes.

A strategy target that increases positive exposure on an ID without a permissible mark stops the run with risk_mark_unavailable after that pulse's decision trace and equity row, so the stop pulse counts as fully valued.
oddity: Unlike valuation stops (C-008), this stop's pulse has an equity row and is the achieved end.
notes: Boundary with subsystem 7 (targets); listed here because it reads the mark plane.

statement: Each pulse records stale_mark_reduction or stale_mark_pass_through risk diagnostics for held or targeted IDs valued at a permissible stale mark.

Stop evidence records affected exposure as the gross absolute quantity times the last reference close (permissible or not) of the stopped IDs, NA when any reference is missing, with basis last_accepted_close_gross.

Every run, sweep candidate and promoted run builds a corporate-action plan from all sealed corporate-action rows of the snapshot under the experiment's policy (research preset by default), in dense and availability runs alike; scheduled dispositions are applied only when availability is active.
oddity: A dense run holding an acquired parent gets cash and quantity checks but never a scheduled disposition (fold-engine.R:539 is inside the availability branch).

statement: Only subtype ordinary_cash_dividend posts cash, only cash/stock/mixed_acquisition dispose, and only stock/mixed_acquisition and spin_off raise quantity effects; any other sealed subtype (for example cash_dividend) has no runtime effect and the summary reports fidelity 'none'.
applies_to_paths: run; resume; sweep; walk_forward; promote; readers
oddity: A held HHH with a sealed cash_dividend row gets no cash; the summary says 'NONE - supplied facts did not affect held instruments'.
notes: The sealing constructor accepts any lower-snake-case subtype (subsystem 1).

statement: Entitlement and effective clocks inside the run's pulse range must equal a pulse exactly or the run refuses with ledgr_corporate_action_clock_mismatch; clocks outside the range resolve to no pulse and the fact never acts.
oddity: A dividend whose entitlement precedes a window but whose posting falls inside it (next_open) never posts in that window.
notes: Known input observation (fixture README) confirmed by reading.

statement: A corporate action becomes due at the later of its posting or effective pulse and the first pulse at or after its knowledge_time; a knowledge pulse after the posting pulse is flagged late_arrival.
applies_to_paths: run; resume; sweep; walk_forward; promote; readers

statement: Dividend cash posts as one CASHFLOW at the entitlement pulse (cash_posting = effective_close) or the pulse after it (next_open), before that pulse's equity and strategy; payment_time is not used.
oddity: The setting is named effective_close but posts at the entitlement clock, not the effective clock.
notes: The fixture puts entitlement on the close before the ex-date, so HHH's $1 posts at s14 while the price drop lands at s15; the synthesis reads the entitlement clock as the ex-dividend boundary (handoff).

statement: In an uninterrupted run the entitled quantity is bound from positions at the end of the previous pulse before that pulse's fills, so a fill executing at the entitlement session's open is not entitled.
design_source: rfc/rfc_equity_settlement_post_v0_2_0_2_synthesis.md 3.4 (a buyer on the ex-date does not receive one)
notes: Probe: buy decided s13 (fill s14 open), entitlement s14 close: no CASHFLOW, final equity 99990.

statement: A resumed run rebuilds entitled quantities for entitlements at or before its start pulse from ledger events stamped strictly before the entitlement time, which includes fills at the entitlement session's open.
oddity: Fresh and resumed runs diverge: the same strategy interrupted after s13 and resumed credits the dividend (final equity 100000 vs 99990 uninterrupted).
notes: Not WS22 byte identity; contradicts the resume-agreement statements in the Persistence Contract and LDG-2980 only for this case. Control (fill at s13 open) agrees.

statement: Cash posts only for a nonzero entitled quantity, as quantity times gross_cash_per_parent_unit, at most once per source fact (posted facts are read back from existing events and duplicates fail closed).
A cash refusal (cash_amount or cash_posting = 'refuse') or quantity refusal (unsupported_quantity = 'refuse') on a held entitlement raises an error, so the run ends FAILED rather than INCOMPLETE.
oddity: The strict preset fails the run (ledgr_corporate_action_unsupported, status FAILED) while a terminal 'refuse' stops it INCOMPLETE (C-026).

statement: Quantity effects of stock and mixed acquisitions and spin-offs never change positions under report_only; recipient instruments are never credited and the summary reports fidelity 'unsupported' with omitted-value estimates.
applies_to_paths: run; resume; sweep; walk_forward; promote; readers
notes: Probe: III keeps 10 shares after the s17 spin-off with no JJJ; DDD disposed for 300 cash with 330 successor value not represented.

statement: A due scheduled acquisition row disposes a held parent at its permissible mark (or frozen close) with basis 'evidence', not at the sealed cash terms; only a last_mark default changes the price, a refuse default stops terminal_settlement_unsupported, and no usable mark stops terminal_mark_unavailable.
oddity: gross_cash_per_parent_unit on a cash_acquisition does not price the disposition: CCC disposes at 49.80 (stale mark age 1) against 50.00 terms.

statement: Scheduled dispositions resolve before lifetime terminals within a pulse, and a refused or unpriced scheduled row stops the run before the lifetime path; precedence is per pulse, so a lifetime terminal effective at an earlier pulse disposes first.
notes: Probe (held_terminal_position = 'refuse'): CCC stops at s19 terminal_settlement_unsupported, status INCOMPLETE.

statement: A held ID whose decision view shows lifetime known_inactive resolves through held_terminal_position by exact sealed terminal_event label or the default entry; an empty label stops terminal_settlement_unsupported|terminal_label_missing.
notes: The known_inactive state itself comes from the provider (subsystem 3).

statement: Terminal prices are: last_permissible = permissible mark; haircut = (1 - h) times the permissible mark; last_mark = last observed close of any age within the window; write_off = 0; a frozen holding under last_permissible or haircut takes frozen_terminal_position instead.

A disposition posts one atomic DISPOSITION event per ID at the pulse close with zero fee, FIFO realization and cash quantity times price; its meta names source, fact, label, choice, basis, policy id and mark provenance, and replay rejects disagreeing rows.
applies_to_paths: run; resume; sweep; walk_forward; promote; reconstruct; readers

statement: A run config without a corporate-action identity resolves every terminal as 'refuse'.
notes: Historical configs only; new configs always carry an identity (backtest-config.R:275-277).

statement: Schema-1 corporate-action or valuation policy records stay readable but executing, resuming, rerunning or promoting into them refuses with ledgr_policy_schema_mismatch.
DISPOSITION and CASHFLOW events are not fills: fills, closed trades, n_trades and win_rate ignore terminal outcomes while equity and realized P&L include them.
oddity: A disposed position never appears as a closed trade (probe: two dispositions, closed trades 0).

statement: The corporate-action summary reports fidelity unsupported over modeled over none over not_supplied, lists every scheduled and lifetime disposition with its assumption label, and estimates omitted value from bar closes at the effective time.
The summary's entitled parent quantity is recomputed from ledger events stamped before the entitlement time, the same rule as resume (C-021), not read from the fold's bound quantity.
oddity: Can disagree with the quantity the fold actually entitled when a fill executes at the entitlement session's open (inferred from C-020/C-021).

statement: Assumed terminal outcomes count lifetime dispositions (including exact-label declared ones) and never scheduled evidence dispositions; the warning names each non-evidence outcome and its declaring argument.

An availability run that reaches the end of its fold, normally or by a typed stop, writes one completion row: intended bounds are the first and last calendar pulses, achieved bounds run from the first pulse to the last fully valued pulse, and complete_performance is true only for DONE.
A soft interrupt (option ledgr.interrupt) or pulse limit writes no completion row, keeps decision diagnostics, commits the equity prefix and leaves the run RUNNING.

Finalization writes an availability run's fold equity facts as the exact achieved prefix together with the terminal status, but a run with zero equity facts (a stop on its first pulse) falls through to dense event replay over every calendar pulse.
oddity: A first-pulse stop stores 26-27 equity rows with NA positions_value and equity although achieved end is NA; ledgr_run_open and a rerun of the same run_id then fail with ledgr_run_terminal_evidence_invalid.
notes: A walk-forward test run in this state cannot be reopened on rerun (C-073; inferred).

statement: Repeating an INCOMPLETE run_id validates the completion row, the exact stored equity prefix and a recorded stop diagnostic, then returns without invoking strategy code.
A RUNNING or FAILED row with a valid completion row is finalized only: its equity prefix is recomputed from ledger holdings and the valuation state, without replaying the fold.

A resume restarts at the pulse after the last stored strategy_state and deletes ledger events stamped at or after the close of the pulse after the restart pulse, and equity, features and state at or after the restart pulse.
oddity: The event cut is on the close clock while version-2 fills are stamped at the next open, so a fill decided at the restart pulse would not be deleted (no committed path writes one; not probed).

statement: Resumed cash, positions and lots are replayed from ledger events stamped at or before the restart pulse close (including fills at that session's open); the corporate-action plan is rebuilt from existing events.
notes: See C-021 for the entitlement divergence this produces.

statement: Opening positions are posted as opening CASHFLOW events at start_ts_utc on the first attempt, or on a resumed row that has no events yet.

Once a run row exists, an error or interrupt without a written terminal status records FAILED with the message and re-raises; an unexpected fold error rolls back the fold transaction and then records an error diagnostic.
Resume refuses when the config hash, metric context, snapshot or execution timing version differ from the stored run (ledgr_run_hash_mismatch, ledgr_execution_timing_version_mismatch).

Availability reconstruction rebuilds equity on the open-session calendar through the last fully valued pulse, valuing holdings at their last observed close in the run window with no horizon check, and rewrites equity_curve.
oddity: The public reconstruction entry point deletes and rewrites persistent equity_curve rows.
notes: Probe (freeze run): rebuilt equity identical to stored over 40 rows.

statement: Reconstruction checks the last rebuilt cash against initial cash plus every ledger cash delta, so an INCOMPLETE run with ledger events after its last valued pulse fails with ledgr_invariant_violation.
oddity: A valuation stop one pulse after a buy decision (fill at the stop session's open) cannot be reconstructed: 'Cash identity violated'.
notes: LTB-0203's stopped case has no event after its last valued pulse.

statement: An INCOMPLETE run keeps fills committed at the stop session's open (decided at the last valued pulse), so last_executed_ts_utc can be later than the achieved end and the stored equity prefix excludes those fills.
oddity: Probe: last valued s13 close, last executed s14 open; the AAA fill is in the ledger but in no equity row.
notes: Readers that replay the ledger after the achieved end (availability positions, walk-forward carry by last equity ts) see or skip it depending on their cutoff.

statement: Reconstruction of an availability run with no fully valued pulse refuses with ledgr_invalid_run.
The diagnostics reader returns the run's stored run_diagnostics rows in diagnostic_seq order; dense runs return the typed zero-row schema.

The availability reader rebuilds, at each diagnostic timestamp, the provider decision view from sealed facts and ledger holdings stamped at or before that time, and recomputes marks from snapshot bars on the run calendar, reapplying the frozen restriction.
notes: Probe: FFF rows at s13-s17 match the fold's frozen and current marks.

statement: For dense runs the availability reader reports every universe ID as member, unrestricted, priced current_close, age 0 and status active at every equity timestamp.

ledgr_run_explain joins one recorded decision row with its availability row and the first execution diagnostic sharing its decision time, defaulting to no_action/no_target_change, and fails ledgr_run_explanation_unavailable without a decision trace.
notes: completion_status is runs.status; complete_performance falls back to status DONE without a completion row.

statement: Fill rows come only from FILL events; their recording_pulse_ts_utc is the fill time for dense runs and, for availability runs, the close of the execution session found through a unique filled diagnostic whose prior session closed at the decision time, else NA.
oddity: Durable runs derive the recording pulse from sessions and diagnostics; sweeps derive it from the execution-opportunity index (sweep.R:1509-1518).

statement: print and summary follow recorded completion evidence: incomplete performance labels return and drawdown as achieved-prefix values and withholds annualized return, volatility and Sharpe.

The valuation summary classifies a run frozen, stale or current from held decision rows' mark_source, reports frozen-at-end value and a long-only total_return_if_frozen_worthless bound, and drops frozen rows at pulses without an equity row from weights.
print and summary emit one assumption warning before metrics whenever any holding froze or any terminal outcome rested on an assumption, with no materiality threshold.
Completion readers (ledgr_run_completion, run info, run list) project the stored completion row and take affected IDs from stopped diagnostics; without a row every field is typed unknown.
ledgr_run_open opens only DONE and INCOMPLETE runs; an INCOMPLETE run must be availability-aware and pass completion, exact equity prefix and stop-diagnostic validation.
oddity: See C-038: a first-pulse stop fails this validation.

statement: ledgr_run_compare rejects explicit non-DONE runs and excludes them otherwise, disclosing attempted, done, incomplete and failed counts.

A sweep candidate runs the shared fold with an in-memory handler, a portable provider built from the snapshot's facts, and the experiment's corporate-action plan, and reaches the same final equity as the durable run.
notes: Probe: one-candidate sweep final equity identical to the run (99958) with dividend, two dispositions and a spin-off.

statement: Availability-aware sweeps refuse compiled spot-FIFO accounting and dense precomputed feature payloads.

A sweep row's status is the fold status (DONE, INCOMPLETE, FAILED) and its completion_json carries the completion record, stopped IDs and the five valuation flags computed from retained in-memory diagnostics.
notes: Memory candidates retain only stale/frozen held decisions, terminal dispositions and stopped rows.

statement: Candidate extraction refuses an INCOMPLETE row (ledgr_incomplete_sweep_candidate) and a FAILED row unless allow_failed = TRUE.
Ranking, review, filtering and selection admit only DONE rows; frozen or assumed-terminal DONE rows stay eligible and carry their flags.
Saved sweeps persist completion_json and INCOMPLETE status, and reopened rows derive the same completion columns.

Promotion refuses INCOMPLETE and FAILED candidates, checks only the snapshot hash, replaces cost and risk with the candidate's, and re-executes through ledgr_run with the experiment's own universe rule, valuation policy, corporate-action policy, opening and scoring range.
oddity: Valuation and corporate-action policy and the universe rule are not part of candidate provenance, so an experiment configured differently from the sweep promotes without refusal (not probed).

statement: Promotion context is written only after the committed run succeeds; a context-write failure warns and keeps the run.
Walk-forward training selection admits only DONE candidates with a finite metric; with no such candidate the no_selection policy reuses previous parameters, runs no test window, or fails.
An INCOMPLETE selected test run marks its fold PARTIAL, keeps its achieved evidence, and ends the carry chain with no later opening state.
Under carry_test_state the next fold opens with the previous test run's last stored equity cash, ledger positions at that timestamp and per-unit lot cost basis; short holdings refuse.
oddity: Carried holdings start the next window with no mark history (C-005), so one without a bar on the window's first pulse stops the test run at once (inferred).
notes: Freeze state and corporate-action entitlement state are not carried.

statement: carry_test_state refuses overlapping, reverse-ordered or gapped test windows before any work, measuring gaps on open-session closes for availability experiments and on universe bar timestamps otherwise.
On a walk-forward rerun an existing DONE or INCOMPLETE test run is opened as recorded; any other existing test run resumes through the ordinary run path with the same window, parameters and seed.
oddity: An INCOMPLETE test run that stopped on its first pulse cannot be opened (C-038, C-059), so its rerun would fail (inferred).

statement: Walk-forward candidate extraction requires a DONE fold with a selected candidate and a test run; PARTIAL folds are not extractable.
